text.p: Israel's Bio-Technology General Corp said on Tuesday it had granted Japan's Rohto Pharmaceutical Co an exclusive license to market its BioLon ophthalmic product for Japan and Pacific Rim countries.
It said in a statement that the pact called for "a payment on signing and future milestone payments" but gave no figures. A Bio-Technology spokesman declined to give a value for the deal.

"Because of Rohto's strength in the ophthalmics field, we are confident that they will be a very effective partner for our product in the licensed territories," Bio-Technology CEO Sim Fass was quoted in the statement as saying.

Rohto specialises in ophthalmic and other agents with 41 percent of its sales in the ophthalmic sector, the statement said. Its eyecare products hold a 35 percent share of the Japanese ophthalmic market.
BioLon is used in ophthalmic surgery such as cataract removal. It is currently marketed in 17 countries.
Bio-Technology is waiting for approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market BioLon in the United States.
Bio-Technology develops, manufactures and markets genetically engineered and other products for human health care.
